newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Jan 24.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Jan 24.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - Trading sputtered early in the week but moderating weather in the eastern half of the U.S. turned things around on Wednesday and Thursday, Random Lengths said in its end-week lumber market review. Some prices dipped early in the week but regained all or most of the ground, the reporting agency said.

Western S-P-F markets led the turnaround, which spilled into other species. Southern Pine showed the most consistent strength though overall activity was off a bit from the robust pace of recent weeks. Green fir prices bucked the firming trend.
December's drop in the rate of new homebuilding, announced on Wednesday, was dismissed as an outgrowth of terrible weather in the West last month, Random Lengths said.

Field inventories remained on the light side and most orders were for quick loads. Distributors and reloaders, who had delayed buying in hopes of a price pullback, were the most consistent buyers, Random Lengths said.
Wholesalers, who came into the week with orders to cover, accumulated small long positions by the end of the week.

Most dealers and treaters remained skeptical of the market's staying power and held invenmtories in check, relying on quick loads from secondaries. Southern mills continued to have problems with logs, particularly the larger sizes needed to produce widths and long lengths, Random Lengths said.
Canada lumber exports as of January 16 were at 11.9 percent of Jan-March quota and 83.4 pct of annual April-March quota.
A hot item was Southern Pine Premium radius edge decking and some buyers offered sharply higher prices to induce production.

The wide widths of dimension were generally more active than the narrows. Boards stayed strong; prices of key 1x12 items posted solid gains, and export demand continued to drive some Southern Pine items higher. Western red cedar producers said they feared losing market share to alternatives, but they bumped up prices to keep pace with rising log costs. Ponderosa industrials were flat to higher, Random Lengths said. (Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8720)
